inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL scalar query constructs a calendar date from a year and ordinal day number with MAKEDATE.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored calendar-ordinal audit. Fixed leap-year, year-end, out-of-range, zero-day, and NULL inputs exercise MAKEDATE's date construction and NULL behavior; the source literal and purpose are not copied.

fixture_notes: Ordinal 60 maps to February 29 in leap year 2024; ordinal 365 maps to December 31 in 2023; ordinal 366 rolls into January 1 of 2024; zero and NULL inputs exercise NULL results.
determinism_notes: Input IDs, years, and ordinal values are fixed, and output is ordered by the primary key with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE calendar_ordinals (input_id INT PRIMARY KEY, calendar_year INT NULL, ordinal_day INT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT input_id, calendar_year, ordinal_day, MAKEDATE(calendar_year, ordinal_day) AS constructed_date, CASE WHEN MAKEDATE(calendar_year, ordinal_day) IS NULL THEN 'invalid-or-missing' ELSE 'valid-date' END AS date_class FROM calendar_ordinals ORDER BY input_id

checks.sql: SELECT input_id, calendar_year, ordinal_day FROM calendar_ordinals ORDER BY input_id
